To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the development of EU policy officers in the French local administration has led to the emergence of a group of actors who have become a key intermediary in the implementation of European policies, but whose practices are not necessarily in line with the objectives of European integration.
the development of EU policy officers is an essential channel for the dissemination of specifically EU standards and skills.

EU policy officers are not the key actors for the development of multi level governance in France and that they do not contribute to the emergence of new modes of governance in the field of EU regional policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the institutional and professional dynamics that shape the practices of EU policy officers in France.
the question of the institutionalization and the limits of the Europeanization of the French local authorities.
the institutionalization of a new category of public officials and the emergence of a new type of public action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of these actors is not an essential channel of the Europeanization of the public sphere in France.

, far from being the privileged actors of Europeanization, the policy officers in the French case are more likely to be a channel of institutional competition between the various levels of government.
these agents are not the key to understanding the Europeanization of the French regional state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the European policy officers' activity is characterized by a tension between the desire to act as a bridge between levels, on the one hand, and the constraints that limit the ability of these professionals to do so, on the other.
these actors are more mediators than brokers, and their practices are more about managing tensions than fostering cooperation.

the development of EU policy officers has been a key factor in the development of multi level governance, but it has also been a factor in the institutionalization and professionalization of local government in France.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the case of French local governments, the development of these agents has not led to a significant increase in the circulation of information and skills between the different institutional levels of government.
, in the absence of a strong Europeanization dynamic, these professionals are not able to overcome the constraints of the institutional framework in which they operate.
, despite their growing number, these professionals are not the main actors in the development of multi level governance in France.
